pageCache.pageTitle: Support for parents – Denmead Infant School
pageCache.text:
Support for parents
Being a parent or carer can be the most wonderful thing in the world and can bring much love and joy into your life. However parenting and family life also comes with challenges. Some of these may be short lived, others may bring longer term difficulties.
Whist as a school we cannot prevent these challenges from occurring or even resolve them all, we will always do our best to listen to parents and carers and signpost you to places where you can access further support.
Let’s Talk!
This is our regular opportunity for parents and carers to meet together, supported by a member of school staff to share the highs and lows of family life. These are generally held on either a Tuesday or Friday morning at 8.45a.m. – details are advertised in our newsletters or available from the school office.
Below are some websites and organisations which we know of. If you come across any others that you would like to share with the school community, then please let us know and we can add them to this resource.
FISH
This is the Hampshire Family Information and Services Hub. It contains information on a wide range of local services including Family Support, Childcare, SEND and a has a directory of local help for those experiencing difficulty.
Please click to access the Family Information & Services Hub:
Ideas to support with your child's learning
We have arange of useful links to help support your child’s learning at home. These can be found at: Denmead Infant School’s Useful Links
Child’s health
It can be tricky deciding whether or not to keep your child off school when they’re unwell.Is my child too ill for school?
Health for kids is aimed at both children and parents and offers support during your child’s primary years.Health for kids
Parenting- including managing behaviour and routines
Welcome to Hampshire County Council’s partnership with the Solihull Approach. These free online courses offer advice and practical tips to boost your confidence as a parent, help you navigate family life and strengthen your relationships. Whether you are a mum, dad, foster parent or grandparent, there is a course for you.Solihull Approach
As a parent or carer, you can take small steps to help your child’s wellbeing as well as your own. You can do this by starting with the basics.Back to basics
Being a parent or carer can be the most wonderful thing in the world and can bring so much love and joy into your life. We also know that the responsibility of parenthood and the daily challenges of this role can be as daunting as they can be exciting.Barnado’s Family Space
Easy ways to eat well and move more.Healthier Families
Mental Health and Wellbeing – child and adult
Confidential help and advice. It’s safe and easy for you to speak to a qualified health professional. Just send a message!Chat Health
Hampshire CAMHS is an NHS specialist service for young people aged 5-18 years and their families who are experiencing difficulties with their mental and emotional health.Hampshire Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service
Family Assist is an innovative new way of ensuring that parents and their friends and families have access to a wide range of information and resources, both local and national, at their fingertips.Family Assist
Mental Wellbeing Hampshire is a partnership of organisations working to support good mental health and wellbeing in our communities.Mental Wellbeing Hampshire
Inourplace is brought to you by an NHS team of psychologists, psychotherapists, and a network of specialist professionals connected to the Solihull Approach. It is a free parent portal that can help support you and your child with moving up to a new school. They also offer various online courses dedicated to improving emotional health and wellbeing in parents, children, teenagers, adults and grandparents. Inourplace
Family Life and relationships
Family Lives provides targeted early intervention and crisis support to families. If you need to talk, we’re here to listen!Family Lives
Understand how to support children during a separation and find out what the law says about parental rights.NSPCC
We provide refuge and community-based support to adults, children and young people affected by domestic abuse in need of advice, support and information tailored to their level of risk and support needs.Stop Domestic Abuse
The Help through Hardship helpline is a free phone service delivered in partnership with Citizens Advice. Our friendly advisers have already helped thousands of people who are worried about money and are here to help you access the support you need.Help Through Hardship Helpline
Bereavement
Family Bereavement: How to support children through grief and loss.Losing a loved one is incredibly hard, especially for children. In this article, we share advice and guidance from our experts to help you support child through the journey of grief and loss.NSPCC
There’s no right or wrong way to feel when someone dies. Everyone experiences bereavement differently. You don’t have to cope on your own, and we’re always here for you.Childline
Supporting young people who have a significant person in their life who has died or is dying.Simon Says
Remember someone in our Memory Meadow.Plant memories that bloom forever by dedicating a flower to your loved one in our virtual Memory Meadow.Winston’s Wish
Hampshire Youth Access (HYA) is a partnership of 11 leading agencies providing counselling, mental health and emotional wellbeing advice and support to children and young people aged 5 – 17 across Hampshire.We also give advice and information to anyone concerned about a child or young person’s emotional wellbeing.Hampshire Youth Access
Our Child Bereavement Support service (known as Rowans Meerkat Service), offers specialist emotional support to children and young people who have a significant adult (such as a parent or grandparent), with a life-limiting illness or, who have been bereaved of an adult close to them. We work alongside families with children up to the age of 18.Rowan’s Hospice Meerkat Service

Early Years Foundation Stage
Welcome to Early Years Foundation Stage…
We have 2 classes in Year R
In EYFS, the children continue to follow the Early Years’ Foundation Stage Curriculum, which outlines the stages of development for children from birth to five years old. At the end of the year they are assessed against the Early Learning Goals, which are the age related expectations for the end of the Reception Year.
Children have the opportunity to explore each area of the curriculum through their own initiated learning (Adventure Time) and teacher led focus activities (Challenges). They also experience learning through whole class teaching, small groups and are supported in developing the learning behaviours needed be independent learners. Teachers plan the provision as a team and then personalise the activities and learning environment to the needs of their children. Each class is supported by a full time teaching assistant.
We keep detailed records of each individual child’s progress and invite parents to Pupil Progress meetings in the Autumn and Spring term as well as sending home Reports of Achievement at the end of each school year.

British Values
Promoting British Values at Denmead Infant School
The Department for Education states that:
“schools should promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.”
Our Denmead Curriculum Aims
Values to ensure a learning adventure
Our Vision for all of our children
Happy together Secure relationships and exemplary pastoral care
Resilience Independence
We are empowering our children to be confident individuals who are able to lead safe, healthy and fulfilling lives.
Growing together Irresistible learning environments where adults and children thrive on challenge
We want our children to grow into responsible citizens who make a positive contribution to local, national and global communities.
Aiming high Achieving excellence for all
Collaboration Respect
We enable our children to develop skills, knowledge, understanding and enjoyment that sustain a lifetime of successful learning.
At Denmead Infant School these values are embedded and reinforced through our everyday ethos and practice:
Democracy
Democracy is promoted across our school. Children are always listened to by all adults and they are taught to listen carefully and with consideration to each other, respecting the right of every individual to have their opinions and voices heard. Children also have the opportunity to share their opinions and ideas through the School Council who regularly discuss these in their meetings and then feedback to their classes. The School Council members are elected by the children, reflecting our British electoral system and demonstrating democracy in action.
The Rule of Law
The importance of laws, whether they are our class or school rules, are consistently reinforced and embedded positively every day. These are taught through assemblies and our PSHE curriculum and they ensure that every child is able to learn in a safe environment. Through our everyday practice and language, our children are taught the value and reasons behind rules and that they are there to keep everybody safe. Through our behaviour mascot, Kindy, children learn the importance of the choices we make to have kind hands, kind feet and kind mouths.
Individual Liberty
Children are actively encouraged to make positive choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. Our children are given the freedom to make choices and are taught how to exercise these safely, examples of these can clearly be seen through our e-safety and PSHE lessons. Whether it is through choice of challenge, how they record their learning or participation in our extra- curricular activities, our children are given the freedom to make choices.
Mutual Respect and Tolerance for others
Respect is embedded through our Denmead Curriculum for Learning, our relationships curriculum, our RE curriculum and our assemblies. The children are taught the importance of respect for all. This is modelled by all staff in their relationships with each other and every child. This is embedded within the school’s inclusive culture and ethos. Children are given the skills and understanding to become respectful members of the wider community. We teach our children that whilst we do not all share the same beliefs or ideas, we should value difference and not judge each other.

Our learning superheroes help us learn!
We want our children to be lifelong learners who leave us both wanting to learn more and with the skills to do so. We use our learning superheroes to teach our children how to be resilient, independent, creative, fearless and collaborative learners. The children are introduced to the superheroes one by one, and are then given feedback on their learning using the superhero language. Everyone celebrates when we see children or adults showing ‘superhero’ behaviours.
Lady Fearless
I initiate activities
I seek challenge
Captain Creative
I find ways to solve problems
Rosie Resilient
I stay focused on an activity
I keep trying even when challenges occur
Teamwork Twins
I can work and play co-operatively
I can take turns
Mr I
I can work without adult support
I can organise myself and my things
I can make my own choices

Home Learning
We appreciate the fact that many of our parents or carers wish to support their children’s learning at home. At Denmead Infant School we use the term home learning to describe activities which we provide for children to complete in partnership with adults or older siblings. This is not the same as the more traditional understanding of ‘homework’ which is a task that a child might be expected to complete by themselves. Below are some of the ways in which you can be involved- if you have any further questions please talk to your child’s class teacher.

Home learning in Key Stage 1 will include:
Reading
Your child will always be given a reading and library book for them to share with you at home. The reading book will be appropriate to the level at which they are reading and we ask that you listen to your child read at least 4 times a week. Remember they do not have to read the whole book each time, just a page or two may be enough for one session and discussing the story and answering questions is just as important as reading aloud.
SEESAW Please encourage your child to record a clip of them reading and send it in to share and celebrate with their class teachers!
The library book allows your child to choose a book that interests them and so they may not be able to read it independently. This offers you the opportunity to read to your child and to talk about the book.
Please use your child’s yellow reading diary to record the books that you have read at home, with comments about the experience.
Phonics
Year 1 children will be learning phonics in school each day. On a Friday the graphemes and common exception words that they have learnt that week will be shared with you on SEESAW as a video. On that day, your child will also bring home two copies of each grapheme and word so that you are able to support and consolidate their learning at home by playing SNAP, matching pairs, flashcards etc.
Spelling
Year 2 children will be learning to spell common exception words in school each day. On a Friday, the words of the week will be shared with you on SEESAW so that you will be able to continue to support your child with independently spelling the words.
Please use the range of activities shared in the Spelling booklet on Seesaw e.g. spelling scribble, spelling triangles, word shapes, cut out letters, writing in sand etc. If your child can already confidently spell the words then please challenge them to write them in sentences. Please share your weekly spelling practise with your class teacher via Seesaw (it could be a video clip, photograph, piece of work etc.).
Fortnightly home learning challenge
Every fortnight, your child will be set a piece of home learning on Seesaw. The objective of this home learning is for you to support your child’s maths or topic learning in a variety of ways. The expected outcome will be made clear in the setting of the task and we ask that you share this outcome with your child’s class teacher on SEESAW every fortnight.
Incidental challenges
Your child’s teacher will use Seesaw at incidental times throughout the year to share learning that has taken place, that your child would benefit with practising outside of the classroom e.g. telling the time, using money, seasonal observations, skipping etc. There is no expectation for you to share any response to these challenges on Seesaw.
Celebration of learning
Your child’s teacher will use Seesaw to share and celebrate your child’s efforts, work and achievements in school. This may be in the form of a video, a photograph or a copy of their work. We ask that you share this with your child and celebrate their achievement with them.
